text:
dina: quick heads-up — seeing spike of ContainerCreating hangs across a us-west3 cohort during the 08:30 attach wave. pods stuck ~20-40s, nvme %util pegged. suspect janitor scrub + writeback backlog colliding with bulk attaches.

ryan: can you paste the small node snippets?

dina: pasted minimal traces from one host:
# iostat -x 1 2
Device r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgqu-sz await %util
nvme0n1 1300 3400 52000 430000 2.7 10.6 98.9

kernel: scrubber[4123]: async scrub start nvme0n1 bucket=11
kernel: nvme0n1: queue depth saturated, throttling
kubelet: attach timeout waiting for ephemeral disk

sre-bot: alert: nvme_util > 95% on cohort us-west3-g sampled hosts

ryan: okay. short-term mitigations we can do now: 1) soft-pause janitor for a small canary subset of the cohort for 15-30m, 2) `ionice -c3` / lower ioprio for scrub threads, 3) apply label `ephemeral.quiet=true` so autoscaler prefers other nodes during the window.

dina: applying soft-pause to subset A and lowering scrub ioprio now. also toggling autoscaler hint prefer_ephemeral_quiet=true for attaches.

sre-bot: action: janitor pause applied to us-west3-g/cohort-4-subsetA at 1735550020
scheduler: info: attach-prefer-quiet policy applied to cohort-4-subsetA

ryan: good. collect `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1` and `nvme error-log` for 3 hosts to check for media errors or thermal events if util stays high after mitigations.

dina: mitigations in place at 1735550030. attach success jumped 67% -> 97% in first 2m on the subset. leaving monitoring for 30m. uploading smart logs to TKT-7890 if anything looks odd.

hw-team: if we still see sustained >90% util after pause, escalate — we'll need firmware check and SMART trend analysis.

ryan: medium-term action items: 1) RFC to integrate autoscaler attach-forecasts with scrub-scheduler (forecast API + push hook), 2) randomize scrub bucket assignment + global jitter to avoid accidental alignment, 3) automated ioprio/ionice lowering when forecast indicates heavy attach waves, 4) cost calc for extended scrub windows vs GPU-minute loss from failed attaches.

dina: agreed. cost note: pausing/staggering scrubs adds some extra IO-hours (~3-6% estimated) but prevents failed attaches and wasted GPU time which looks much more expensive during heavy waves. include precise calc in RFC.

sre-bot: ticket created TKT-7890 "us-west3-g attach delays correlated with scrub IO saturation"

dina: creating RFC for scrub-scheduler/scheduler integration and will canary the change after review. will post postmortem if pattern repeats.
